speaker: Unknown
en: The second answer is the cost of intelligence is coming down so rapidly that even if that is not true today, it's going to be true in six or 12 months.
zh: 第二个答案是，智能的成本正在快速下降，即使今天这一点不成立，六到十二个月后也会成立。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like it's a 10x cost reduction per year, roughly speaking, for the same intelligence.
zh: 大致来说，同样的智能水平，成本每年下降约 10 倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's something we tell our founders not to worry about too much because it will just solve itself with time.
zh: 这是我们告诉创始人们不用太担心的事情，因为随着时间推移它自己会解决。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think an engineer today with a model is like, yeah, 1000x better than an engineer without AI.
zh: 我认为今天一个工程师配上模型，比没有 AI 的工程师好大概 1000 倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: Would you not use it?
zh: 你会不用它吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think a year ago it might have been reasonable to say, well, a given engineer for a particular task might be more cost effective than a model.
zh: 我想一年前这么说或许还算合理：就某项特定任务而言，某个工程师可能比模型更有成本效益。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there is no chance that it's true today if you're using the absolute best intelligence.
zh: 但我认为，如果你用的是绝对最强的智能，今天这已经完全不可能成立了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I'd probably go that far.
zh: 是的，我大概也只敢说到这个程度。

speaker: Unknown
en: I just don't think there's a single programming task that a human is more effective for a human to do than a model to do.
zh: 我只是认为，不存在任何一个编程任务，由人类来做会比由模型来做更有效。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hello, thanks for this opportunity.
zh: 你好，感谢这个机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of countries, especially in Eastern Europe, have underdeveloped startup stage and underdeveloped startup communities.
zh: 很多国家，尤其是东欧国家，初创阶段和初创社区都不发达。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you have any tips on building especially a community of founders, like not being a founder of a startup, but being a founder of a community?
zh: 对于建设一个创始人社区，你有什么建议吗？就是不是作为初创公司的创始人，而是作为一个社区的创始人？

speaker: Unknown
en: How to build from scratch?
zh: 如何从零开始建设？

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks.
zh: 谢谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was going to say move to SF.
zh: 我本来想说：搬到旧金山去。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you want to optimize the chance of your startup, you should probably join an existing community versus having to create it from scratch.
zh: 如果你想最大化你初创公司的成功几率，你可能应该加入一个现有的社区，而不是从零开始创建一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you cannot go to SF, of course that's the biggest place to build a startup, but go to London or Paris where there is at least a critical mass of startups so that you can surround yourself with great founders.
zh: 如果你不能去旧金山——那当然是做初创公司最大的地方——那就去伦敦或巴黎，那里至少有初创公司的临界规模，这样你就可以让自己身边都是优秀的创始人。

speaker: Unknown
en: That are going to make you better founders.
zh: 他们会让你成为更好的创始人。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you are the only one in a city, it's very difficult because you don't have any peers to push you forward.
zh: 如果你是所在城市里唯一的一个人，那会非常困难，因为你没有任何同伴来推动你前进。

speaker: Unknown
en: And like the people who don't understand your life are going to hold you back.
zh: 而那些不理解你生活方式的人会拖你的后腿。

speaker: Unknown
en: Gray and I sort of experienced this.
zh: Gray 和我算是经历过这种事。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I started a company in 2011 called GoCardless.
zh: 我在 2011 年创办了一家叫 GoCardless 的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: It did Y Combinator and actually came back to London.
zh: 它参加了 Y Combinator，实际上后来回到了伦敦。

speaker: Unknown
en: Gray was like our number two hire or something like that.
zh: Gray 大概是我们的第二号员工还是之类的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Number three hire.
zh: 第三号员工。

speaker: Unknown
en: And GoCardless, and a small number, but really less than five companies were the kernel of the London startup ecosystem.
zh: 而 GoCardless，加上少数几家公司——其实不到五家——就是伦敦初创生态的核心。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can kind of trace from GoCardless this family tree to many, many, many dozens of other companies.
zh: 你几乎可以从 GoCardless 这棵家谱树追溯到几十家其他公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And TransferWise is in there, Monzo is in there, and it's kind of amazing how it spreads.
zh: TransferWise 在里面，Monzo 也在里面，这种传播方式挺神奇的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in those early days,
zh: 但在那些早期日子里，

speaker: Unknown
en: So the direct answer is find a really great startup that embodies the startup culture and join that.
zh: 所以直接的答案是：找到一家真正优秀的、体现了初创文化的公司，加入它。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in the early days of any great startup, it feels like a cult.
zh: 但在任何一家伟大初创公司的早期，它感觉像一个邪教。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like it feels like you believe something that no one else believes.
zh: 就是感觉你相信一些没有其他人相信的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you said it out loud outside the room, people would laugh at you almost.
zh: 而且如果你在房间外面把它说出来，人们几乎会笑话你。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you like have these collective set of beliefs and behaviors and ways of working that make you extremely effective.
zh: 但你们拥有这一整套共同的信念、行为方式和工作方式，让你们极其高效。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I just try and find that basically.
zh: 所以我基本上就是建议去找那样的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the reality is there is always going to be one global hub for startups.
zh: 而现实是，永远会有一个全球性的初创公司中心。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that will attract the most ambitious people and the companies that are going after the biggest vision.
zh: 它会吸引最有雄心的人，以及那些追逐最大愿景的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you probably want to be there.
zh: 而你可能就想在那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't stop there being other smaller regional hubs.
zh: 这并不意味着不存在其他更小的区域性中心。

speaker: Unknown
en: But for a lot of companies and for the most ambitious founders, you definitely should be considering San Francisco at the very least.
zh: 但对于很多公司，以及最有雄心的创始人来说，你至少绝对应该考虑旧金山。

speaker: Unknown
en: My question would be related to the thing you've spoken about, the artifacts we should be pumping into AI.
zh: 我的问题和你讲过的那个话题有关，就是我们应该持续投喂给 AI 的那些资料（artifacts）。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we as founders should pump everything we could possibly find to AI.
zh: 也就是我们作为创始人，应该把我们能找到的一切都投喂给 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: Investors would be doing the same thing.
zh: 投资人也会做同样的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you think that we leave too much judgment to AI and where is that gap where we should stop and leave our judgment to us and not outsource it to AI?
zh: 你觉得我们是否把太多判断交给了 AI?那个鸿沟在哪里——我们应该在哪里停下来,把判断留给自己,而不是外包给 AI?

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you.
zh: 谢谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so, I mean, there are many ways to answer your question.
zh: 是的,我的意思是,有很多种方式可以回答你的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we can't answer all of it, like, for sure.
zh: 我认为我们肯定无法回答全部。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, one thing I've been arguing with Nico during the batch is how much AI should write for us, because I think there is a direct correlation between the amount of thinking you do and how you write.
zh: 比如,这一批里我一直在和 Nico 争论的一件事是,AI 应该替我们写多少东西,因为我认为你思考的量和你写作的方式之间存在直接关联。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I've personally been writing most of the things I've been writing so that I don't delegate too much to the AI.
zh: 所以我个人一直是自己写大部分我要写的东西,这样我就不会把太多东西委托给 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's one thing.
zh: 这是一件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other thing that we've been talking about...
zh: 我们一直在讨论的另一件事……

speaker: Unknown
en: is I feel like at YC there is so much emphasis on how AI can give superpowers to partners and therefore can be shared with founders and that's been the most mind-blowing thing I've experienced at YC is the speed at which this organization built tools to empower all of the people who go there.
zh: 是我感觉在 YC,人们非常强调 AI 如何给合伙人赋予超能力,进而可以与创始人分享,这是我在 YC 经历过的最令人震撼的事情——这个组织构建工具来赋能所有来到这里的人的速度。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think though that something that's super important for YC as an organization is to think about the thing that AI is not going to be able to replace.
zh: 不过我认为,对 YC 作为一个组织来说,非常重要的一点是思考 AI 无法取代的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there are a few things like, you know, founder wellbeing is incredibly important and putting more emphasis on how can we help founders take care of themselves.
zh: 有一些事情,比如,创始人的身心健康极其重要,我们应该更加重视如何帮助创始人照顾好自己。

speaker: Unknown
en: Community is also something where, you know, AI is not going to help.
zh: 社区也是 AI 帮不上忙的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Knowledge sharing is something where AI has, where YC has a unique thing where you have
zh: 知识共享是 AI……是 YC 拥有独特优势的地方,因为你有——

speaker: Unknown
en: 200 companies that are obsessing over how to make the most out of AI.
zh: 200 家公司都在绞尽脑汁地思考如何把 AI 的价值发挥到极致。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there will never be content available on the latest thing you can do, but you're surrounded with people that are obsessing over this.
zh: 关于你能做的最新事情,永远不会有现成的内容可用,但你身边围绕着一群正在为此绞尽脑汁的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so one of the things we've been talking about is not...
zh: 所以我们一直在讨论的事情之一,不是……

speaker: Unknown
en: Not obsessing too much over what the AI can do in order to empower all of you, but also what is AI not able to do and how do you make sure that you're excellent at it?
zh: 不要过度纠结于 AI 能做什么来赋能你们所有人,同时也要思考 AI 不能做什么,以及如何确保你在那些事情上做到卓越?

speaker: Unknown
en: Because sometimes I feel like you can be blindsided if you're only looking at it in one way.
zh: 因为有时我感觉,如果你只从一个角度看问题,你可能会被蒙在鼓里。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the next months, everything can be done internally.
zh: 在接下来的几个月里,一切都可以在内部完成。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, every tool can be built internally and instantly.
zh: 我的意思是,每个工具都可以在内部即时构建。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is the purpose of B2B products anymore?
zh: 那 B2B 产品还有什么意义呢?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like if you can build everything by yourself, so then everything that matters is just critical infrastructure.
zh: 就像如果你可以自己构建一切,那么所有重要的东西就只剩下关键基础设施了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what will happen with B2B products?
zh: 所以 B2B 产品会怎样?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I broadly agree with the premise of your question, but I would reframe it more as a spectrum than a binary.
zh: 我大体上同意你问题的前提,但我想把它重新表述为一个光谱,而不是非此即彼。

speaker: Unknown
en: One or the other.
zh: 二选一。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the reframe I would take is like, what's the hard bit?
zh: 我想采用的重新表述是:难的那一点是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like your startup has to have a hard bit.
zh: 就像你的创业公司必须有一个“难的那一点”。

speaker: Unknown
en: And 10 years ago, writing a lot of software was in and of itself, the hard bit.
zh: 而十年前,编写大量软件本身就是那个难的那一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is not hard anymore.
zh: 那已经不再难了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you have to have other things to be hard, to like, to have any kind of durability, you have to have something that's hard.
zh: 所以你必须有其他东西是难的,才能——要拥有任何形式的持久性,你必须有某种难的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that might in some cases just be like brutally hard B2B sales into some industries.
zh: 而这有时可能就是向某些行业做极其艰难的 B2B 销售。

speaker: Unknown
en: Others, it might be a regulatory barrier, like getting a banking license almost killed me.
zh: 另一些情况下,可能是监管壁垒,比如拿到银行牌照差点要了我的命。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's pretty hard.
zh: 那是相当难的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or figuring out the physics of like spaceship launch, pretty hard.
zh: 或者搞清楚宇宙飞船发射背后的物理学,相当难。

speaker: Unknown
en: Actually, most hardware in and of itself is just like hard.
zh: 实际上,大多数硬件本身就很难。

speaker: Unknown
en: The atoms add the hard bit.
zh: 原子增加了难的那一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I'd just be thinking, like, on my spectrum of, like, this is very, very easy versus very, very hard, I'd, like, I'd just shy away from the easier end of the spectrum and just, like, pick bits that are harder and more ambitious because it will make your startup more durable.
zh: 所以我只会这样思考:在“非常非常容易”与“非常非常难”这个光谱上,我会避开光谱上更容易的那一端,去选择那些更难、更有雄心的部分,因为这会让你的创业公司更有持久性。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I would just absolutely not start something like Calendly today or Partyful or maybe Partyful actually has a network effect, but certainly Calendly or, like, DocuSign.
zh: 所以我今天绝对不会去做类似 Calendly 或 Partyful 这样的东西——不过 Partyful 实际上可能有网络效应,但 Calendly 或类似 DocuSign 这样的东西肯定不行。

speaker: Unknown
en: Basically dead.
zh: 基本上已经死了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like I think really pure software is just not, it's just too easy to replicate now.
zh: 就像我认为纯软件真的不行,现在复制起来太容易了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So just ask yourself, where's the hard bit?
zh: 所以问问自己:难的那一点在哪里?

speaker: Unknown
en: You're recording office hours, you're recording interviews, right?
zh: 你们在录制 office hours,你们在录制面试,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: It seems like you're trying to do, like, what you're trying to do is to make Y Combinator an AI-native company, right?
zh: 看起来你想要做的,是让 Y Combinator 成为一家 AI 原生公司,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: What happens when the AI is a better YC general partner than you are, right?
zh: 那,当 AI 成为比你更好的 YC 普通合伙人时,会发生什么,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: What are you going to do?
zh: 你会怎么做?

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you going to be selling Birkin bags or what?
zh: 你要去卖铂金包吗,还是怎么样?

speaker: Unknown
en: As Mathilde said, we're going to be therapists.
zh: 正如 Mathilde 说的,我们要去做心理咨询师。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so I think there are, like, first, what I said I really believe in, which is there are so many things that the AI will not be able to do.
zh: 是的，我觉得，首先，是我真正相信的一点，就是有很多事情是 AI 做不到的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, just so you know, and I think Nico can tell the story as well, is there is a new feature that's being experimented right now with YC where you can book an office hour with a virtual partner.
zh: 就比如说，我想 Nico 也可以讲这个故事，就是 YC 现在正在试验一个新功能，你可以和一个虚拟合伙人预约办公时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you can literally, like Nico was able to do an office hour with himself.
zh: 所以你真的可以，就像 Nico 能够和他自己进行了一次办公时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: Apparently it was really weird.
zh: 据说那真的很怪异。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was awkward.
zh: 那确实很尴尬。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think there is a part of it which is like, you know, therapists, community builders.
zh: 所以我觉得有一部分就是，你知道的，治疗师、社区营造者这类。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there is also, Gary Tan wrote an excellent post a few weeks ago about the power of witnessing, which is the fact that you have someone in the room with you that acknowledges that what you're going through is something that's normal, is incredibly powerful, it's an incredibly lonely job, and a robot doing this is not as helpful.
zh: 但还有，Gary Tan 几周前写了一篇非常棒的文章，讲的是“见证”的力量，也就是说，房间里有一个认可你正在经历的事情是正常的人，这是极其有力量的，这是一份极其孤独的工作，而一个机器人来做这件事就没那么有帮助。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's not just like the human community and well-being and all this.
zh: 所以这不仅仅是人类社群和幸福感之类的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I also think that there is a power of witnessing.
zh: 我也认为存在“见证”的力量。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I also think one of probably a misconception, I have new eyes on this because I was a recent partner,
zh: 我还认为其中可能有一个误解，我对此有新的视角，因为我是一个刚加入的合伙人，

speaker: Unknown
en: You might think that at the scale YC has a lot of advice is advice that they give to everyone.
zh: 你可能以为在 YC 这个规模下，很多建议是给所有人统一给出的建议。

speaker: Unknown
en: The reality is I feel like partners go really deep in understanding specifically your business, your market, et cetera, so that they can give tailored advice.
zh: 实际上，我感觉合伙人们会非常深入地了解你的具体业务、你的市场等等，这样他们才能给出量身定制的建议。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so even if you have a database of 7,000 companies, there is still so much that we don't know about your company specifically and that partners need to do a good job at understanding.
zh: 所以即使你有一个 7000 家公司的数据库，仍然有很多我们不了解的、你这家公司特有的东西，需要合伙人去很好地理解。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's always fun to get like a fresh eyes on our job.
zh: 能以全新的视角看待我们的工作，总是很有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: But maybe one last thing on that.
zh: 但也许关于这个再说最后一件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: All the partners at YC are past successful founders themselves who actually did YC.
zh: YC 的所有合伙人本身都是过去成功的创始人，他们自己都真正经历过 YC。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there is that, maybe that's the witnessing, we know what you are going through because we did it ourselves.
zh: 这就是，也许这就是“见证”，我们了解你正在经历什么，因为我们自己经历过。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's a huge difference with a lot of investors out there who have never been founders before, who don't know what you're living.
zh: 这和市面上很多从没当过创始人、不了解你所经历的生活的投资人相比，是一个巨大的区别。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that piece is never going to disappear and cannot be replaced by AI.
zh: 我认为这一块永远不会消失，也无法被 AI 取代。

speaker: Unknown
en: So thank you for your talks.
zh: 谢谢你的分享。

speaker: Unknown
en: My question was regarding research in AI startups, because in my personal case, I've built a startup while I'm doing like a PhD, okay, in which I research like things for improving the product and all this stuff.
zh: 我的问题是关于 AI 创业公司中的研究的，因为就我个人的情况来说，我在读博士的同时创办了一家创业公司，好吧，我在研究一些改进产品的东西以及所有这类事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how to know in each moment if it's like better to
zh: 那么如何在每个时刻判断，是

speaker: Unknown
en: Focus on their own research for improving this product or focusing more on business like to scale, get more clients and all this stuff.

zh: 你觉得——你认为主观能动性是一种真的可以培养的特质吗,是一块可以练的肌肉,还是说天生有没有就是有没有?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think high agency is basically a belief that your actions are going to produce output, like you actually are going to have impact.
zh: 我认为主观能动性基本上是一种信念:相信你的行动会产出成果,就像你真的会产生影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if I were trying to develop that in myself or trying to teach a child to do that, I think I would point them towards projects that seemed hard enough to push them, but tractable enough that they could actually
zh: 如果我要在自己身上培养它,或者试图教一个孩子做到这一点,我想我会引导他们去做那些看起来足够难、能推动他们的项目,但又足够可操作,让他们真的能够

speaker: Unknown
en: Like see some output and then just like continually make that harder and harder and harder.
zh: 比如看到一些产出,然后就不断地把难度越提越高、越高越高。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I just like pick something that seems quite difficult and try it.
zh: 所以我就是挑一件看起来相当难的事情,然后去试。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that might be a side project.
zh: 那可能是一个业余(side project)项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to keep yourself going, I would probably try and find a co-founder.
zh: 为了让自己坚持下去,我可能会去找一个联合创始人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And at some point this would look like doing a startup, right?
zh: 而到某个时候,这看起来就是在做一家创业公司了,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like find a friend who thinks really, really smart and determined and together see what...
zh: 比如找一个你觉得非常、非常聪明又有决心的朋友,然后一起看看……

speaker: Unknown
en: Come up with an idea of a side project to build that seems like quite difficult, but probably not totally, totally impossible.
zh: 想出一个要做的业余项目点子,它看起来相当难,但可能又不是完全、完全不可能。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then do that and see how it went.
zh: 然后去做,看看结果如何。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then just like, if that succeeds, do another one and another one.
zh: 然后就像,如果成功了,就再做下一个,再下一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And eventually you're like, you end up building rocket ships to Mars.
zh: 最终你就会——你最后就造出飞往火星的火箭了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's sort of how it goes.
zh: 事情差不多就是这样发展的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like no one actually realistically starts by building rocket ships to Mars, right?
zh: 毕竟现实中没有人真的是从造飞往火星的火箭开始的,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: They build Zip2 and then they build PayPal and then they build Tesla and then eventually they build the really big thing.
zh: 他们先做了 Zip2,然后做了 PayPal,然后做了 Tesla,最后才做成那个真正宏大的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think that's in the abstract how I would approach that problem.
zh: 所以从抽象层面讲,我会这样去处理那个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I was going to say, I think you, I don't think you can teach it, but I think you can get better at it.
zh: 是,我正想说,我不认为你能教出来,但我认为你可以越做越好。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's pretty much what you described.
zh: 这基本就是你描述的内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you have the kernel there, new, some small core from which you can expand, you can train yourself.
zh: 如果你心里有那颗种子——一个可以向外扩展的小小内核——你就可以训练自己。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very good.
zh: 这说得很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, Lukasz here.
zh: 好,这里是 Lukasz。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I see this strange phenomenon in SF recently that every billboard and every plane and every balloon
zh: 我最近在 SF(旧金山)看到一个奇怪的现象:每一块广告牌、每一架飞机、每一个气球上

speaker: Unknown
en: Brex, is a tech company nowadays.
zh: Brex,如今都是一家科技公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And since building everything became so easy, there's this funny thing that companies just try to gather traction regardless of what they do.
zh: 而且既然做东西变得这么容易,就有个好玩的现象:公司不管做什么都只是想攒热度(traction)。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm just curious, how do you think about standing out in the crowd when you build companies?
zh: 所以我只是好奇，当你创建公司时，你是如何思考在众多竞争者中脱颖而出的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because way more companies are being built, at least at the early stages nowadays.
zh: 因为如今被创建的公司多得多,至少在早期阶段是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had a nice talk from the Brex CEO, where he was saying that, so Brex in SF, if you've been in SF, I don't know, six years ago or something, SF was covered with Brex ads, and he was basically saying the reason, at the point they just bought all the billboards in San Francisco, and the way he was justifying it was no one was doing it, so just want to stand apart, and in order to stand apart, gonna buy billboards.
zh: 我们听了 Brex CEO 的一场很棒的分享,他说的是——Brex 在 SF,如果你几年前,大概是六年前左右在 SF 的话,SF 满城都是 Brex 的广告,他基本上是在解释原因:在那个时点他们直接买下了旧金山所有的广告牌,他给出的理由是没有人在这么做,所以就想显得与众不同,而为了与众不同,就去买广告牌。

speaker: Unknown
en: And clearly now billboards are another thing that can make you stand apart.
zh: 而显然现在,广告牌又成了另一件能让你脱颖而出的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the job of a founder every time is to think about how you can differentiate.
zh: 所以创始人的工作每次都是去思考你要如何做出差异化。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if the answer was obvious, then everyone would do it.
zh: 如果答案是显而易见的,那所有人都会去做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, you know, this is what you need to obsess over and you'll always have an answer that's better for your company specifically.
zh: 所以,你知道,这就是你需要为之痴迷的东西,而且你总是会得到一个对你的公司本身而言更好的答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's an issue that every billboard in SF is about AI.
zh: 我觉得 SF 满城广告牌都是关于 AI 的,这确实是个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: During my time, all the billboards were teched already.
zh: 在我那个年代,所有广告牌早就都是科技公司(tetched,原文如此)的了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's always been the case in SF.
zh: SF 一直都是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's an industry town.
zh: 它是一座行业城市。

speaker: Unknown
en: You go to LA, every single billboard is about a TV show or a movie.
zh: 你去洛杉矶,每一块广告牌都是关于某部电视剧或电影。

speaker: Unknown
en: The US has industry towns in a way that Europe doesn't so much.
zh: 美国有「行业城市」,而欧洲没那么多。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I really like Mathilde's answer, which is like,
zh: 但我真的很喜欢 Mathilde 的回答,就是——

speaker: Unknown
en: Distribution matters more than ever.
zh: 分发(distribution)比以往任何时候都更重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's clearly true.
zh: 这显然是真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the way to get distribution, the metagame is evolving so quickly, you've just got to figure something out for yourself.
zh: 而获得分发的方式——这个元游戏(metagame)进化得非常快,你必须自己琢磨出一套东西来。

speaker: Unknown
en: The Cluelay founder found a way to get reach and distribution.
zh: Cluelay 的创始人找到了获得触达和分发的方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: I do agree that distribution is more and more and more important than it ever was because it's one of the hard things.
zh: 我确实同意,分发比以往任何时候都越来越重要,因为它是难点之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: Software no longer is the hard thing about building the company.
zh: 软件不再是从头建立公司的难点所在了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Distribution can be one of the hard things.
zh: 分发可能是很难的事情之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: But remember what minigame you're playing now?
zh: 但要记住你现在玩的是哪个小游戏吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're at the very early stage, you are playing the minigame of getting towards product market fit, right?
zh: 如果你处在非常早期的阶段,你玩的是走向产品市场契合的小游戏,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like finding some first customers and figuring out from them what they need and building that and then getting to the point where you need to put fuel on that fire and scale it.
zh: 比如找到一些首批客户,从他们那里弄清楚他们需要什么,把他们需要的东西做出来,然后到达需要往这团火上浇燃料并把它规模化的阶段。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so when you're looking at those billboards and how companies that have product market fit are getting their customers, remember they're playing a completely different game.
zh: 所以当你看着那些广告牌、看着那些已经实现产品市场契合的公司是怎么获得客户的时候,记住,他们玩的是完全不同的游戏。

speaker: Unknown
en: The way that you stand out from them to an individual customer is by giving them like real like white glove service by like turning up in person, spending an inordinate amount of time for what is like a small contract and building something that exactly fits their needs.
zh: 你在面对单个客户时脱颖而出靠的是,比如提供真正的白手套式服务,比如亲自登门,为一份小合同花费不成比例的大量时间,并且打造一个完全契合他们需求的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the like unscalable thing that allows you to compete with somebody that's putting up a billboard on the highway in San Francisco.
zh: 这就是那种无法规模化的东西,让你能够和那些在旧金山高速公路上竖广告牌的人竞争。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks everyone.
zh: 谢谢大家。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you.
zh: 谢谢。
